{{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = [[Governor of North Dakota|Governor]] | before_election = [[Doug Burgum]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Kelly Armstrong]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in North Dakota}} The '''2024 North Dakota gubernatorial election''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect the [[governor of North Dakota]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Doug Burgum]] decided to not seek a third term and [[Doug Burgum 2024 presidential campaign|ran for president]]. North Dakota is a Republican stronghold, and the [[North Dakota Democratic–Nonpartisan League Party|Democratic–Nonpartisan League (NPL) Party]] has not won a gubernatorial race in the state since [[1988 North Dakota gubernatorial election|1988]]. The Republican nominee, U.S. representative [[Kelly Armstrong]], was elected to his first term, defeating the Democratic–NPL nominee, state senator [[Merrill Piepkorn]] in a landslide. Armstrong was sworn in to office in December 2024, succeeding Burgum, who was subsequently appointed [[United States Secretary of the Interior|Secretary of the Interior]] by [[Donald Trump]] following Trump's victory in the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. {{toclimit|3}} ==Background== In November 2022, voters in the state approved a constitutional amendment limiting governors to two four-year terms, but it only applies to individuals elected after January 1, 2023, so incumbent governor [[Doug Burgum]] was still eligible to run for re-election under a [[grandfather clause]].{{Cite web |last=MacPherson|first=James |date=November 8, 2022 |title=North Dakota voters OK term limits for governor, legislators |url=https://apnews.com/article/bismarck-north-dakota-term-limits-government-and-politics-ebba348663d0a8e715f9b90714602354 |access-date=November 20, 2022 |work=Associated Press News}} On June 7, 2023, Burgum announced that he would instead [[2024 Republican Party presidential primaries|run for the Republican nomination]] for [[president of the United States]] in [[2024 United States presidential election|2024]], a race he dropped out of on December 4, 2023. Despite considering running for a third term after the end of his presidential campaign, Burgum announced he would not run for a third term on January 22, 2024. Before Burgum's announcement, former state Senator and former [[2018 United States House of Representatives election in North Dakota|congressional candidate]] [[Tom Campbell (North Dakota politician)|Tom Campbell]] suggested at and considered a gubernatorial run, despite whatever choice Burgum made.{{cite web |last1=Thaden |first1=Geoff |title=Tom Campbell Poised to Enter Governor's Race Regardless of Doug Burgum's Decision on Reelection |url=https://www.wdayradionow.com/news/regional-news/71640-tom-campbell-poised-to-enter-governors-race-regardless-of-doug-burgums |publisher=[[WDAY (AM)]] |access-date=26 January 2024 |date=4 January 2024}}{{cite web |last1=Port |first1=Rob |title=Port: Former state Sen. Tom Campbell sounds like he's ready to be governor |url=https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-former-state-sen-tom-campbell-sounds-like-hes-ready-to-be-governor |work=[[The Forum of Fargo-Moorhead]] |access-date=26 January 2024 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20231215005734/https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-former-state-sen-tom-campbell-sounds-like-hes-ready-to-be-governor |archive-date=15 December 2023 |date=15 December 2023 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription}} After the decision from Burgum to not seek re-election, Campbell entered the race.
